Ammonium chloride has been promoted for self administration as a diuretic, for example in premenstrual water retention; an oral dose of 650 mg three times daily for up to 6 days has been sug- gested, but such use is generally considered inappropriate. Profile Benproperine is used as a cough suppressant in non-productive cough (p.1547). It is reported to have a peripheral and central action and has been given in usual oral doses of 25 to 50 mg two to four times daily as the phosphate. Benproperine embonate has been used similarly.
